paragraphs: Rabbi Chananyah, son of Rabbi Ivi.

One exposition of his is mentioned in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:2: the text does not say, “How beautiful are your steps in a sandal,” but “in sandals”—two sandals: a closing at Passover and at the Festival.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The wordplay links sandals (נעלים) with closings (נעילה). The consulted continuation discusses seasonal opening and closing at Passover and the autumn Festival; it does not warrant inserting special Neilah prayer services into this abbreviated notice.

The checked Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:2 passage names Rabbi Chananyah, son of Rabbi Ivi, and contrasts one sandal with two sandals. Its continuation connects the Passover and autumn Festival closings with seasonal opening and closing. The notice is therefore not expanded into a claim about special Neilah prayer services.
